name: Counter / color picker
spec: Build a single-page color picker. Show a row of six color swatch buttons (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple), each a <button class="swatch"> with a data-color attribute and its background set to that color. Below them render a 200px square <div id="preview"> and a label <div id="color-name"> showing the current color name. Clicking a swatch sets the preview square's background to that color and updates the label text.
assertions: Six .swatch buttons exist, each with a data-color attribute.
Clicking the green swatch sets #preview background-color to green.
#color-name text updates to the clicked color name.
Clicking a second swatch replaces the previous color.

name: Todo list
spec: Build a todo list app. An <input id="new-todo"> and an "Add" button (or Enter key) append a new <li> to <ul id="todo-list">. Each li contains a <input type="checkbox" class="toggle">, the todo text in a <span class="text">, and a <button class="delete">. Checking the checkbox adds a "done" class to the li (unchecking removes it). Clicking delete removes the li. Persist the full list (text + done state) to localStorage under key "todos" on every change and restore it on load.
assertions: Type 'milk' and press Enter -> an li containing 'milk' exists.
Clicking a checkbox toggles the .done class on its li.
Clicking .delete removes the li.
After reload, todos and their done states persist from localStorage.
Empty input does not create a todo.

name: Markdown previewer
spec: Build a two-pane markdown previewer. Left pane: <textarea id="editor">. Right pane: <div id="preview">. On every keystroke, render the markdown to HTML in the preview. Implement a minimal parser supporting: # and ## headings, **bold**, *italic*, `inline code`, [text](url) links, and unordered lists (- item). Sanitize or escape raw HTML in the input so <script> never executes.
assertions: Typing '# Hi' renders an <h1> containing 'Hi' in #preview.
Typing '**bold**' renders a <strong> element.
Typing '- a\n- b' renders a <ul> with two <li>.
Preview updates live on input without a submit button.
Input '<script>alert(1)</script>' does not execute and is visible as text.

name: Habit tracker grid
spec: Build a habit tracker. Seed five habits (e.g. Water, Exercise, Read, Meditate, Sleep). Render a table where each row is a habit name followed by 7 checkboxes for the last 7 days (label columns with day abbreviations). Clicking a checkbox toggles that day's completion. After each row show a <span class="streak"> with the current consecutive-days streak ending today. Persist to localStorage key "habits".
assertions: Grid has 5 rows x 7 checkboxes.
Clicking a checkbox toggles its checked state.
Checking today and yesterday shows a streak of at least 2.
Unchecking today drops the streak to 0.
State persists across reload.

name: Kanban-lite board
spec: Build a kanban board with three columns: Todo, Doing, Done, each a <section class="column" data-col="todo|doing|done">. An input at top adds a new card to Todo. Each card is a <div class="card"> containing its text and two buttons <button class="move-left"> and <button class="move-right"> that move the card one column left/right (buttons disabled/hidden at the ends). Show a count badge in each column header.
assertions: Adding 'task A' creates a .card in the todo column.
move-right moves the card to doing, then done.
move-right is unavailable in the done column.
Column count badges update after moves.

name: Pomodoro timer
spec: Build a pomodoro timer. Display mm:ss in <div id="clock"> starting at 25:00 in Focus phase. Buttons: <button id="start">, <button id="pause">, <button id="reset">. When the timer hits 00:00 it auto-switches to a 5:00 Break phase (show phase name in <div id="phase">), then back to Focus. Update document.title to 'mm:ss - Phase' every second. Reset returns to 25:00 Focus. Pause must actually stop the countdown (no leaked intervals).
assertions: Start begins the countdown; clock decrements once per second.
Pause freezes the clock value.
document.title contains the current time and phase.
Reset restores 25:00 and Focus phase.
After the focus timer reaches 0, phase becomes Break at 5:00 (test may use a shortened duration via console or wait).
No double-speed ticking after start-pause-start.

name: Form wizard
spec: Build a 3-step form wizard. Step 1: name (required) and email (required, must contain '@'); Step 2: pick a plan via radio buttons (Free/Pro/Team, required); Step 3: confirmation summary showing all entered values, with a Submit button that shows 'Submitted!' and hides the form. A Next button advances only when the current step validates; on failure show per-field error messages in <span class="error"> elements. A Back button returns without validating.
assertions: Next on empty step 1 shows error messages and stays on step 1.
Valid name+email advances to step 2.
Step 3 summary contains the entered name and chosen plan.
Back from step 2 returns to step 1 preserving entered values.
Submit shows 'Submitted!'.

name: Expense tracker
spec: Build an expense tracker. A form with amount (number, required), category select (Food/Transport/Fun/Other), and note adds a row to a <table id="expenses"> with a delete button per row. Show the running total of visible rows in <div id="total">. A category filter <select id="filter"> with an 'All' option filters the table and updates the total. Below, render a bar chart as inline SVG (<svg id="chart">) with one <rect> per category scaled to that category's filtered total. Persist rows to localStorage key "expenses".
assertions: Adding 12.50 Food creates a table row and updates #total.
Deleting a row subtracts it from the total.
Filtering to Food hides non-Food rows and updates #total.
#chart contains one rect per category with nonzero width for categories that have expenses.
Rows persist across reload.

name: Mini e-commerce storefront
spec: Build a mini storefront as a single HTML file with hash routing. Route '#/' shows a grid of at least 6 products (name, price, image placeholder). Clicking a product navigates to '#/product/<id>' with details and an 'Add to cart' button. A cart button in the header opens a <div id="cart-drawer"> listing items with quantity +/- controls and a running total. '#/checkout' shows a form (name, address) whose submit renders an order-success message and empties the cart.
assertions: #/ renders at least 6 product cards.
Clicking a product navigates to its detail route.
Add to cart adds the item; cart total reflects it.
Cart drawer opens and closes.
Quantity + increases line total.
Checkout submit shows success and clears the cart.

name: Multi-page notes app
spec: Build a notes app. Left sidebar lists note titles; clicking one opens it in an editor pane (title input + body textarea, auto-saves on input). 'New note' button creates an empty note; a delete button removes the selected note. A search box filters the list by title/body substring. Each note supports comma-separated tags; a tag filter dropdown shows only notes having that tag. Persist everything to localStorage key "notes".
assertions: New note appears in the list and is editable.
Typing in the body auto-saves (visible after reselecting the note).
Search 'foo' hides non-matching notes.
Tag filter narrows the list correctly.
Delete removes the note.
Notes persist across reload.

name: Quiz with timer
spec: Build a quiz app with 5 embedded multiple-choice questions (4 options each, correct answers pinned in the fixture). A 'Start quiz' button begins; each question shows for 15 seconds with a visible countdown <div id="timer">. Selecting an option locks it and advances on click of Next, or auto-advances unanswered when time expires. After the last question show a score screen 'X / 5' and a review section listing each question, the correct answer, and the user's answer with a .correct/.wrong class.
assertions: Start shows question 1 and a decrementing timer.
Answering a question and pressing Next advances.
Timer expiry auto-advances.
Score screen shows the correct computed score.
Review marks correct and wrong answers.

name: Dashboard shell
spec: Build a dashboard shell with a fixed left sidebar containing nav links Overview, Data, Settings. Clicking a link swaps the main content area (client-side, no reload). Overview: three stat cards with numbers. Data: a <table id="data-table"> with at least 8 rows of fixture data. Settings: a form (display name, theme select) that saves to localStorage and shows 'Saved'. Style it like a real dashboard: sidebar, header, card grid.
assertions: Sidebar nav switches the visible page without reload.
Overview shows 3 stat cards.
Data page table has >= 8 rows.
Settings save persists theme to localStorage and shows 'Saved'.

name: Spreadsheet-lite
spec: Build a 10x10 spreadsheet. Render a table with column headers A-J and row headers 1-10; each body cell is editable (contenteditable or input) with id like cell-A1. Cells display computed values but retain raw input shown while editing (focus shows raw). Support formulas starting with '=': =SUM(A1:A5) over a rectangular range, =A1+B2 arithmetic with +/-/*// of cell refs and numbers, and plain values otherwise. Recalculate dependents when a referenced cell changes. Invalid formulas display '#ERR'.
assertions: Entering 5 in A1 shows 5.
A2=3, A3==A1+A2 displays 8.
B1==SUM(A1:A3) displays 16.
Changing A1 to 10 updates A3 and B1.
=SUM(ZZ) shows #ERR.

name: Canvas drawing app
spec: Build a drawing app on a <canvas id="board">. Dragging the mouse draws freehand strokes. A palette of >= 5 color swatches sets stroke color; a range input sets brush size 1-40. An Undo button removes the last stroke (maintain an undo stack of stroke objects, re-render on undo); a Clear button empties the canvas and stack. Undo is disabled when the stack is empty.
assertions: Dragging paints pixels on the canvas (canvas is non-blank after a stroke).
Selecting a color changes subsequent stroke color.
Undo removes the most recent stroke only.
Clear blanks the canvas and disables Undo.

name: Music step-sequencer
spec: Build a 16-step drum sequencer. A grid of 4 instrument rows (kick, snare, hat, clap) x 16 step buttons; clicking a step toggles .on. Play/Stop buttons and a BPM input (default 120). While playing, highlight the current step column (.playing class) advancing at the BPM, and synthesize each instrument with WebAudio oscillators/noise (no audio files). Stop halts playback and clears the highlight.
assertions: Grid renders 4x16 toggleable steps.
Clicking a step toggles .on.
Play advances the .playing column over time.
Changing BPM changes step rate.
Stop removes the highlight and stops scheduling.

name: Checkers vs random-move AI
spec: Build checkers (8x8, dark squares playable) where the human plays red moving up and the AI plays black. Click a piece then a legal destination; enforce legal moves including mandatory captures and multi-jumps; crown kings at the far row. After each human move the AI picks uniformly at random among its legal moves (prefer captures when mandatory). Show a move counter and declare 'Red wins'/'Black wins' when a side has no legal moves.
assertions: Board renders 12 red and 12 black pieces.
Illegal moves are rejected (piece stays).
A forced capture is enforced when available.
After a human move the AI makes a legal reply.
Reaching the far row crowns a king.

name: Chat UI with fake latency
spec: Build a chat UI. <div id="messages"> scrollable message list, <input id="composer"> and Send button. On send, append the user message immediately with a 'pending' class (optimistic); after a simulated 800ms latency mark it 'sent'. Randomly fail ~25% of sends: mark the message 'failed' and attach a Retry button that re-sends it. After each successful send, a bot reply 'Echo: <text>' arrives ~1s later. Auto-scroll to bottom on new messages only if the user is already near the bottom; otherwise show a 'New messages' pill.
assertions: Sending appends the message immediately as pending.
After latency the message becomes sent and a bot echo arrives.
A failed send shows Retry; retrying re-sends it.
Scroll pins to bottom when already at bottom.
When scrolled up, new messages do not move the scroll and the pill appears.

name: Notion-lite block editor
spec: Build a block editor. The document is a list of blocks rendered into <div id="doc">, each block a contenteditable element. Typing Enter splits the block at the caret into a new block below; Backspace at the start merges with the block above; Backspace on an empty block deletes it. Typing '/' at the start of a block opens a slash menu (Heading, Bulleted list, Todo) that converts the block type; markdown shortcuts work too: '# ' converts to heading, '- ' to bullet, '[] ' to todo. Up/Down arrows move caret between blocks. Persist the block tree to localStorage key "doc".
assertions: Enter in the middle of a block splits it into two blocks.
Backspace on an empty block deletes it and moves caret up.
Typing '# Hello' creates an h1-styled block.
'/' opens the slash menu and selecting Bullet converts the block.
Blocks persist across reload.

name: Figma-lite canvas
spec: Build an infinite-canvas shape editor. A <canvas id="stage"> (or transformed div) supports panning via middle-mouse or space+drag and zooming via wheel (zoom centered on cursor). Toolbar buttons create rectangles and ellipses at the viewport center. Click selects a shape (selection outline + 4 corner handles); dragging moves it; dragging a corner handle resizes it; Delete key removes the selection. A zoom indicator shows the current zoom percent and a 'Reset view' button restores 100%/origin.
assertions: Creating a rectangle renders it on the canvas.
Click selects it showing handles.
Drag moves the shape; handle drag resizes it.
Wheel zoom changes the zoom indicator.
Pan moves the view; Reset view restores it.
Delete removes the selected shape.

name: Video player with custom controls
spec: Build a video player with fully custom controls. Source the <video> from a generated or embedded clip (e.g. canvas.captureStream recorded to a blob, or a small data-URI mp4 you embed) so no network is needed. Controls bar: play/pause toggle button, seek bar showing buffered/playhead position with click-to-seek, current-time/duration readout, volume slider, playback-rate selector (0.5x/1x/1.5x/2x), fullscreen button. Keyboard shortcuts: space toggles play, left/right arrows seek -/+5s, 'f' fullscreen, 'm' mute. Hide controls after 2s of mouse inactivity during playback.
assertions: Play starts playback and toggles the button state.
Seek bar click changes currentTime proportionally.
Rate selector changes playbackRate.
Space toggles playback; right arrow seeks forward 5s.
Time readout matches video.currentTime.
